object.title: Equality of the Terwilliger and orbit centralizer algebras for the conjugacy scheme of the symmetric group
object.statement:
Let $O_1,\dots,O_M$ be the orbits of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)^2$ under $\operatorname{Iso}_1(n)$, and let $B_i$ be the corresponding zero-one matrices. Let $\mathfrak{T}$ denote the Terwilliger algebra of the conjugacy scheme of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$, and let $\mathfrak{B}=\langle B_i:i=1,\dots,M\rangle$. **Equality conjecture.** The matrices $B_i$, $i=1,\dots,M$, form a basis of $\mathfrak{T}$; equivalently, as $\mathbb{C}$-algebras,

$$
\mathfrak{T}=\mathfrak{B}.
$$

The preceding discussion establishes the inclusion $\mathfrak{T}\subseteq\mathfrak{B}$, while the reverse inclusion is described as reasonable but substantially more difficult to prove. Thus the equality remains open in the source.
object.source_name: Mathieu Bogaerts and Peter Dukes, “Semidefinite programming for permutation codes”, arXiv:1212.1185 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2012).

object.title: The arc-weighted second neighborhood conjecture
object.statement: Let $D$ be an arc-weighted digraph without loops or two-cycles. For each vertex $v$, let $\delta_v$ be the second-neighborhood weight minus the first-neighborhood weight, as defined from the arc weights. **Arc-weighted second neighborhood conjecture.** Every arc-weighted digraph $D$ without loops or two-cycles contains a vertex $v$ such that $\delta_v\geq 0$. The paper proves this conjecture for arc-weighted tournaments, while the general arc-weighted statement remains open.
object.source_name: Tyler Seacrest, “The Arc-Weighted Version of the Second Neighborhood Conjecture”, arXiv:1212.1883 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1883

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2012). “That is, consider a minimum digraph $D$ such that $D$ has a vertex-weight function $\eta$ so that it is a counterexample to the second neighborhood conjecture.”

object.title: Sarwate's conjecture on Fourier coefficients of power permutations
object.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic $2$ with $q=|L|$, and let $f(x)=x^s$ be a power permutation of $L$. Define its Fourier coefficients by

$$
\widehat f(a)=\sum_{x\in L}\mu(ax+f(x)).
$$

**Sarwate's conjecture.** If $[L:{\mathbb F}_2]$ is even, then

$$
\sup_{a\in L}\widehat f(a)\geq 2\sqrt q.
$$

The source identifies this as Sarwate's main global conjecture and explicitly says that it is still open; it follows discussion of results proving an earlier characteristic-two conjecture.
object.source_name: Yves Aubry and Philippe Langevin, “On a conjecture of Helleseth”, arXiv:1212.6553 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6553

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012).

object.title: The graph C*-algebra classification conjecture by filtered ordered K-theory
object.statement: Let $E$ be a graph and let $C^*(E)$ be its graph $C^*$-algebra. Suppose that $C^*(E)$ has finitely many ideals, and write ${\mathsf{FK}^+_{\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(E))}\left(C^*(E)\right)}$ for its filtered, ordered $K$-theory. **Graph C*-algebra classification conjecture.** Graph $C^*$-algebras $C^*(E)$ with finitely many ideals are classified up to stable isomorphism by their filtered, ordered $K$-theory ${\mathsf{FK}^+_{\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(E))}\left(C^*(E)\right)}$. The conjecture is a proposed classification of graph $C^*$-algebras by $K$-theoretical invariants. It remains open, and some results suggest that an additional condition of finitely generated $K$-theory may be necessary.
object.source_name: Søren Eilers, Gunnar Restorff and Efren Ruiz, “Classification of graph C*-algebras with no more than four primitive ideals”, arXiv:1212.6750 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6750

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012).

object.title: Daykin–Häggkvist conjecture on completing dense partial Latin squares
object.statement: Let $P$ be an $n\times n$ partial Latin square in which each symbol, row, and column contains at most $\frac{1}{4}n$ nonblank cells. **Daykin–Häggkvist conjecture.** Every such partial Latin square can be completed to a Latin square. This is a central completion problem for partial Latin squares and is linked to Nash-Williams's conjecture on triangle decompositions; the source does not provide evidence of resolution.
object.source_name: Padraic Bartlett, “Completions of epsilon-dense partial Latin squares; quasirandom k-colorings of graphs”, arXiv:1306.0342 (2013).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1205.1558](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1558).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0342

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2013).

object.title: Refined left Gog–GOGAm trapezoid equienumeration conjecture
object.statement: For each $n,k$, consider left Gog and GOGAm trapezoids of shape $(n,k)$, and let $X_{1,1}=l$ denote their bottom entry. **Refined left Gog–GOGAm conjecture.** For each $n,k,l$, the $(n,k)$ left Gog and GOGAm trapezoids with bottom entry $X_{1,1}=l$ are equienumerated. This refines the unweighted left-trapezoid conjecture by requiring equienumeration separately at every fixed bottom-entry value; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Philippe Biane and Hayat Cheballah, “Inversions and the Gog-Magog problem”, arXiv:1401.6516 (2014).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1209.4799](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4799).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6516

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

object.title: Galvin's biregular homomorphism conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph, let $d_u$ denote the degree of $u\in V(G)$, and let $H$ be a loop-graph. Write $\hom(G,H)$ for the number of graph homomorphisms from $G$ to $H$. **Galvin's biregular homomorphism conjecture.**

$$
\hom(G,H)\le \prod_{uv\in E(G)}\hom(K_{d_u,d_v},H)^{1/(d_ud_v)}.
$$

This would extend the regular and biregular homomorphism inequalities, as well as the bipartite case of Kahn's irregular independent-set conjecture. Its status is open.
object.source_name: Yufei Zhao, “Extremal regular graphs: independent sets and graph homomorphisms”, arXiv:1610.09210 (2017).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1512.06398](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06398), [arXiv:1307.5919](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.5919), [arXiv:1205.2718](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.2718).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09210

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2016). “The conjecture remains open for all $d\ge 4$ and $q \ge 3$.”

object.title: Equidistribution of the descent and cycle bistatistics with the excedance bistatistic
object.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $\\{1,2,\ldots,n\\}$, and let $\operatorname{des}_2$, $\operatorname{cyc}$, $\operatorname{pex}$, $\operatorname{des}$, and $\operatorname{exc}$ denote the statistics defined in the paper. Two bistatistics are **equidistributed** on $S_n$ when they have the same joint distribution. **Equidistribution conjecture.** The two bistatistics

$$
(\operatorname{des}_2,\operatorname{cyc})
$$

and

$$
(\operatorname{pex},\operatorname{cyc})
$$

are equidistributed on $S_n$. This conjecture proposes a joint refinement of the preceding equidistribution results for these permutation statistics; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Jean-Luc Baril and Sergey Kirgizov, “Transformation à la Foata for special kinds of descents and excedances”, arXiv:2101.01928 (2021).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1201.4317](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.4317).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.01928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: Ohba's conjecture on list chromatic number
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph. Write $\chi(H)$ for its chromatic number and $\chi_L(H)$ for its list chromatic number.

**Ohba's conjecture.** If

$$
|V(H)|\leq 2\chi(H)+1,
$$

then

$$
\chi_L(H)=\chi(H).
$$

This conjecture concerns when the list chromatic number agrees with the ordinary chromatic number for graphs whose order is bounded in terms of their chromatic number. The source attributes it to Ohba; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Yaser Rowshan, “On generalized list -free colorings of graphs”, arXiv:2201.06029 (2022).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1211.1999](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.1999).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06029

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: The 2-balanced double tree decomposition conjecture
object.statement:
A **double tree** is a graph formed by taking two trees on the same vertex set, with the two edge sets regarded as distinct even when they join the same pair of vertices. A **double tree decomposition** partitions the edges of a double tree into two trees. Such a decomposition is **$k$-balanced** if, at every vertex, the absolute difference between its degrees in the two trees is at most $k$.

**2-balanced double tree decomposition conjecture.** Any double tree has a $2$-balanced double tree decomposition.

The paper proves that every double tree has a decomposition that is $4$-balanced, improving the previously known bound of five. Examples are known that admit a $2$-balanced decomposition but no $1$-balanced one, so the conjectured bound would be best possible; the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Freddie Illingworth, Emil Powierski, Alex Scott and Youri Tamitegama, “Balancing connected colourings of graphs”, arXiv:2205.04984 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.04984

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

object.title: Eliahou–Villarreal conjecture on projective dimension of edge ideals
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertices $V(G)=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$, let $R=\mathbb{K}[x\mid x\in V(G)]$, and let $I(G)=(x_ix_j\mid \{x_i,x_j\}\in E(G))$ be its edge ideal. The quotient $R/I(G)=\mathbb{K}[\Delta_G]$ has a 2-linear resolution when its minimal graded free resolution has the form

$$
0 \longrightarrow R(-2-p)^{\beta_p} \longrightarrow \cdots\longrightarrow R(-3)^{\beta_1} \longrightarrow R(-2)^{\beta_0} \longrightarrow R \longrightarrow \mathbb{K}[\Delta_G] \longrightarrow 0.
$$

**Eliahou–Villarreal conjecture.** If the edge ideal of a connected graph $G$ has a 2-linear resolution, then

$$
\operatorname{pdim}(R/I(G))=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}\{\deg_G(x_i)\}.
$$

By Fröberg's theorem, the 2-linear-resolution hypothesis is equivalent to $G$ being co-chordal in the convention used here. The paper states that this conjecture is false in general and constructs counterexamples; it also proves the equality for several subclasses, including sequentially Cohen–Macaulay co-chordal graphs and graphs with a full vertex.
object.source_name: Chwas Ahmed, Amir Mafi and Mohammed Rafiq Namiq, “Sequentially Cohen-Macaulay Co-Chordal Graphs: Structure and Projective Dimension”, arXiv:2205.07059 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.07059

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: The almost-stable Kneser hypergraph colorability bound
object.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal G$ be a hypergraph over the ground set $[n]$, and let $r\geq s\geq 2$. Write $\mathcal G_{\widetilde{\{s\text{-stable}\}}}$ for the corresponding almost-stable restriction, let $\operatorname{KG}^r(\mathcal G_{\widetilde{\{s\text{-stable}\}}})$ be its $r$-uniform Kneser hypergraph, let $\chi$ denote chromatic number, and let $\operatorname{cd}^r(\mathcal G)$ denote the $r$-colorability defect. **The almost-stable Kneser hypergraph conjecture.** Every such hypergraph satisfies

$$
\chi\left(\operatorname{KG}^r\left(\mathcal G_{\widetilde{\{s\text{-stable}\}}}\right)\right)\geq\left\lceil\frac{\operatorname{cd}^r(\mathcal G)}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture is proposed in the paper as a partial answer to a problem concerning how large the gap between the colorability-defect bound and the chromatic number can be. The supplied text gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Saeed Shaebani, “Concerning Two Conjectures of Frick and Jafari”, arXiv:2206.00836 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00836

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

object.title: Generic codimension additivity for subdivisions of graphical-model supports
object.statement:
Assume that $\dim(\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}})=d$. Let

$$
h=\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}(G)}h_{\mathcal{X}_C,y_C}.
$$

Let $\sigma$ be the subdivision of $\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$ induced by $h$, and let $\sigma_C$ be the subdivision of $\pi_C(\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}})$ induced by $h_{\mathcal{X}_C,y_C}$. For $z\in\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$, let $k_z$ and $l_z$ be the codimensions of the minimal faces of $\sigma$ and $\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$ containing $z$, respectively. For each $C\in\mathcal{C}(G)$, let $k_{z,C}$ and $l_{z,C}$ be the codimensions of the minimal faces of $\sigma_C$ and $\pi_C(\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}})$ containing $z_C$, respectively.

**Generic codimension additivity conjecture.** If $\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$ and all tent functions $h_{\mathcal{X}_C,y_C}$ are sufficiently generic, then

$$
k_z-l_z=\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}(G)}k_{z,C}-\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}(G)}l_{z,C}.
$$

The preceding corollary proves only the corresponding inequality for the subdivision codimensions. The generic equality is presented as a conjectural strengthening and concerns the combinatorics of intersections of clique-wise regular subdivisions.
object.source_name: Kaie Kubjas, Olga Kuznetsova, Elina Robeva, Pardis Semnani and Luca Sodomaco, “Log-concave density estimation in undirected graphical models”, arXiv:2206.05227 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05227

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

object.title: Mubayi–Rödl conjecture for the Turán density of the tight 5-cycle
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_5^3$ be the $3$-uniform tight cycle of length $5$, with vertex set $\{1,\dots,5\}$ and edges of the form $\{x,x+1,x+2\pmod 5\}$. Let $\pi(\mathcal{C}_5^3)$ denote its Turán density. **Mubayi–Rödl conjecture.**

$$
\pi(\mathcal{C}_5^3)=2\sqrt{3}-3.
$$

The conjecture is attributed to Mubayi and Rödl and is presented as a central open problem on tight-cycle Turán densities; the paper proves results for sufficiently long tight cycles but does not settle the length-$5$ case.
object.source_name: Nina Kamčev, Shoham Letzter and Alexey Pokrovskiy, “The Turán density of tight cycles in three-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2209.08134 (2023).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1201.4326](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.4326).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.08134

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

object.title: The bridge characterization conjecture for double-multiplicity friends-and-strangers graphs
object.statement:
Let $X$ be a connected simple graph, and let $c^{(X)}$ and $c^{(\mathsf{Star}_n)}$ be multiplicity lists, with equal total capacity. Let the center of $\mathsf{Star}_n$ have multiplicity

$$
k=c^{(\mathsf{Star}_n)}_{\varnothing}.
$$

A **$k$-bridge** is a bridge of the relevant multiplicity determined by the center multiplicity $k$. Let $\operatorname{\mathsf{FS_{m,m}}}(X,\mathsf{Star}_n)$ be the double-multiplicity friends-and-strangers graph. **The bridge characterization conjecture.** The graph $\operatorname{\mathsf{FS_{m,m}}}(X,\mathsf{Star}_n)$ is connected if and only if $X$ contains no $k$-bridge in which all vertices have multiplicity $1$. This would extend the paper's connectivity characterizations for single-multiplicity friends-and-strangers graphs to the double-multiplicity setting.
object.source_name: Aleksa Milojevic, “Connectivity of Old and New Models of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs”, arXiv:2210.03864 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03864

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Merkulov–Willwacher's injectivity conjecture for oriented graph cohomology
object.statement:
Let $d$ be an integer, and let $\textsf{OGC}_{2d+1}^{{\:\raisebox{3pt}{\text{\circle*{1.5}}}}}$ be the oriented graph complex and $\textsf{RGC}_d^{{\:\raisebox{3pt}{\text{\circle*{1.5}}}}}(\delta+\Delta_1)$ the ribbon graph deformation complex, with the morphism

$$
\textsf{OGC}_{2d+1}^{{\:\raisebox{3pt}{\text{\circle*{1.5}}}}}\longrightarrow \textsf{RGC}_d^{{\:\raisebox{3pt}{\text{\circle*{1.5}}}}}(\delta+\Delta_1)
$$

induced by the Chas–Sullivan morphism. **Merkulov–Willwacher's conjecture.** The induced map on cohomology is injective:

$$
H^{{\:\raisebox{3pt}{\text{\circle*{1.5}}}}}(\textsf{OGC}_{2d+1})\longrightarrow H^{{\:\raisebox{3pt}{\text{\circle*{1.5}}}}+1}(\textsf{RGC}_d(\delta+\Delta_1))
$$

is injective. This concerns the relationship between oriented graph cohomology and the cohomology of ribbon graph complexes; the paper later indicates that the conjecture is proved using results relating these complexes to moduli spaces of curves.
object.source_name: Alexey Kalugin, “Oriented Getzler-Kapranov complexes and framed curves”, arXiv:2210.16267 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16267

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Transversality criterion for quantum gauge theories
object.statement:
Let ${\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Q}}}$ be a quantum gauge theory with Feynman rule $\Phi$. Let $\mathfrak{i}_{\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Q}}}$ be its quantum gauge symmetry ideal and let $\mathscr{D}$ be its quantum gauge symmetry differential. The theory is called **transverse** when its physical amplitudes satisfy the corresponding quantum gauge symmetry condition.

**Transversality criterion.** The condition

$$
\mathscr{D}\left(\mathfrak{i}_{\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Q}}}\right)\in\operatorname{Ker}(\Phi)
$$

is equivalent to transversality of the theory.

This connects the algebraic quantum gauge symmetry structure with the physical transversality condition and is intended to encode the relevant cancellation identities on Feynman graphs. The supplied text gives no evidence that the criterion has been proved or refuted.
object.source_name: David Prinz, “Renormalization of Gauge Theories and Gravity”, arXiv:2210.17510 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17510

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Bounded-rank characterization by bounded alternation rank
object.statement:
Let $
C$ be a hereditary graph class. **Bounded-rank alternation conjecture.** The class $
C$ has bounded rank if and only if there is $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every first-order formula is equivalent on $
C$ to a formula of alternation rank $k$. This conjecture generalizes the theorem preceding it in the source and relates the structural notion of rank to a uniform bound on quantifier alternation; the source leaves it as a conjecture for future work.
object.source_name: Jakub Gajarský, Michał Pilipczuk, Marek Sokołowski, Giannos Stamoulis and Szymon Toruńczyk, “Elementary first-order model checking for sparse graphs”, arXiv:2401.16230 (2025).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1211.5823](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5823).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16230

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

object.title: Noel's extremal complete multipartite graph conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic graph with at most $mk$ vertices, and let $K_{m*k}$ denote the complete $k$-partite graph with $m$ vertices in each part. **Noel's conjecture.**

$$
\chi_\ell(G) \leq \chi_\ell(K_{m*k}).
$$

The conjecture asserts that this balanced complete multipartite graph maximizes list chromatic number among the specified $k$-chromatic graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1211.1999](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.1999).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

object.title: The global linkage characterization conjecture for rigid graphs
object.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a rigid graph and let $u,v\in V$. A pair of vertices is **globally linked** if every generic realisation of $G$ determines the distance between its two vertices. **Global linkage characterization conjecture.** The pair $\\{u,v\\}$ is globally linked in $G$ if and only if either $uv\in E$ or $u$ and $v$ are joined by three internally disjoint paths in some ${\mathcal{RM}}$-connected component of $G$. This would characterize when two vertices in a rigid graph are globally linked; the corresponding result is known when the whole graph is ${\mathcal{RM}}$-connected, but the general rigid-graph case remains open.
object.source_name: Bill Jackson and J. C. Owen, “The number of equivalent realisations of a rigid graph”, arXiv:1204.1228 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1228

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).
